source_event.summary: Independent audit rejected a ready handoff because executable negative evidence was only declared and canonical access-scope risks were dropped before saturation.

generalized_learning.generalized_failure_pattern: A delivery packet can look complete when validators trust declared passed controls or declared risk applicability instead of re-deriving obligations and binding each adversarial claim to executable hashed evidence.
generalized_learning.plausible_wrong_implementation: Permit a matrix entry to say passed with a narrative evidence label, or permit a canonical access-scope requirement to disappear before risk classification.
generalized_learning.prevention_rule: Extract restrictive access language into canonical risk flags and require structured, head-bound, hashed negative-control evidence before a requirement can be considered saturated.
generalized_learning.detection_rule: Re-derive canonical risk applicability from requirement closure and reject negative-control declarations that lack exact evidence ID parity, procedure, expected/observed outcome, material head and matching SHA-256 bytes.

transfer_cases.scenario: A synthetic release flow declares a negative reference-liveness control passed but omits structured evidence.
A synthetic authenticated active-scope requirement is present in closure while the attack matrix omits authorization and tenant-isolation.
